dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine, how can I help you this morning?

Hey, yeah, good morning. So I'm calling about the storm drain on our corner. It backed up during that storm, Sunday into Monday, and the water went right into the basement where I live. Well, not where I live, the house. I'm the tenant. And it's still not draining, it's Wednesday.
Okay. A storm drain backing up, water into the basement. Let me get the address first.
688 Thames Street. Down the south end, past the Wellington side, Fifth Ward.
688 Thames Street. And the drain is right at the corner by the house?

Yeah, the one on the corner, the catch basin. It's wicked clogged. Like there's sand and leaves packed right up on the grate, you can see it from the sidewalk. And when all that snow started melting with the rain Sunday night it just had nowhere to go. It ran right across the yard and came in through the bulkhead door.
Through the bulkhead. How much water are we talking about down there?

About three inches. Monday morning it was about three inches across the whole floor. Ileana, she owns the place, she came and got me and we were bailing and running the shop vac for hours. Their camping gear got soaked, all the tents and sleeping bags and that, and the chest freezer was sitting in it. We don't even know if the freezer's alright yet.
I'm sorry. So, overnight Sunday into Monday the twenty-sixth, water came in the bulkhead door, roughly three inches, camping gear and a chest freezer got wet. Do I have that right?

Yeah, that's right. And it's not just us. The next two houses down, they had water in their cellars too. I was talking to the guy next door yesterday, he was hauling stuff out to the curb. So it's the drain. It's gotta be the drain. And honestly, that thing's been looking like that since the fall. Leaves sitting on it for months. Nobody ever comes by and does anything with it.
So three houses with water, yours and the two next to you. That's helpful for the crew to know, that tells them it's the basin and not one house.

Right, that's what I'm saying. And I'm kind of fed up, you know? Like it's Wednesday now. The storm ended Monday. There's still a big puddle sitting in the gutter right over the grate, it's just sitting there. If it rains again this week it's gonna go right back in the bulkhead. So I need somebody to come out and actually clear it. Like right away, not in a couple weeks.
I hear you. Let me pull up the schedule, can you hang on one second for me?
Yeah, sure.

[pause] Okay, thanks for waiting. The crews are still going corner to corner from Monday, there's a lot of these backed up all over the city after all that melt. The earliest I can get someone out to your corner is Friday, the thirtieth.
Friday. [pause] That's two more days of it just sitting there. There's nothing sooner? Three basements got water, that doesn't bump it up at all?

I'm going to put in the notes that it's affected three homes, and that the water's still standing over the grate. That does matter to them. But Friday is what I've got on the board right now, and I'll put it down as a priority.
Alright. I mean, I guess. It's just, you know, nobody's looked at that thing in forever and now we're the ones scrubbing the floor. It's kind of annoying, honestly. Sorry, I'm not yelling at you.
No, you're fine. Can I get your name for the work order?
Doug Gifford. G-I-F-F-O-R-D.
Doug Gifford, G-I-F-F-O-R-D. And a good number to reach you if the crew needs to get hold of somebody?
Yeah, my cell, 401-555-0193. I rent the in-law unit over the garage, so I'm usually around. Ileana and her wife are working all day, that's why I'm the one calling.

401-555-0193. Okay. And just to read it all back to you, Doug. 688 Thames Street, catch basin at the corner backed up during the storm Sunday into Monday. Water came in the bulkhead door, about three inches in the basement, camping gear and a chest freezer wet. The two neighboring houses also had water in their cellars. Grate is packed with sand and leaves and there's still standing water over it. Crew to check and clear it Friday the thirtieth.

Yeah. That's all of it. [pause] Sorry, there's this patch of sun on the kitchen table and it keeps sliding around every time I move. Must be the window catching off a car or something. Anyway. Yeah. That's everything.
Well, at least the sun's out today. If anything changes before Friday, if it gets worse or more water comes in, call us back and reference Thames Street and I'll find it.
Okay. I just really hope somebody actually shows up Friday, 'cause if it rains before then we're doing this whole thing over again.
It's on the list for Friday. I put the three houses right at the top of the notes.
Alright. Thanks, Lorraine.
You're welcome, Doug. Take care.
